title: Source shift gauge for flat telescope normalization
statement: Let f: Z → Y be proper between Noetherian schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], with derived categories in a common localization universe [def-pc-derived-category], F = derivedPullback f [def-pc-derived-pullback], a supplied strong monoidal structure [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], and additive termwise tensor pullback H [def-pc-module-pullback]. Put Q = Qh_Y and G = H followed by Qh_Z. Fix a counit ε: Q⋙F → G making F a left derived functor, and a coherent integer shift on F for which ε commutes with shifts. There exist e: F(O_Y[1]) ≅ O_Z[1] and a natural automorphism a of Q⋙F such that, for each concrete flat telescope P [def-sc-flat-telescope-stage-map] and X=q(P), a_(X[1]);commShift_(Q⋙F)(X) = F(commShift_Q(X));b(Q(X));a_X[1], where b(K)=F(c_Y(K) inverse);δ_F(O_Y[1],K);(e tensor id);c_Z(F(K)), and c is the canonical shift-unit comparison [def-sc-scheme-canonical-shift-unit-iso]. The assertion is only about the shift gauge on the source functor; no comparison with G, invertibility of ε components, or extension of the equation beyond telescopes is part of its conclusion.

proof.text: Construct the local gauge components on flat telescope shift representatives, with stage-map naturality and the equation on literal telescopes. This is the local supplied-tensorator model calculation, without any global natural automorphism.

The source functor Qh followed by derived pullback inverts homotopy quasi-isomorphisms. For any map between model representatives, use a common stage-map refinement a;s=b. Precompose the desired naturality square with the invertible image of a, apply model naturality to a and b and cancel. This proves naturality for every map between representatives.

For any complex P take the compatible bounded-flat tower resolving its good truncations. Let a be the sum of the augmentations to P and φ one minus transition. Compatibility gives φ;a=0. The cone desc map with zero shifted component augments the literal telescope to P. Its two cone restrictions and the flat truncation telescope comparison prove it is a quasi-isomorphism. Applying the quotient gives a resolution of every homotopy object by a telescope representative.

Extend the hom components of the local gauge through the full resolving class using exists_natTrans_from_resolvingClass, applied with both functors equal to Qh followed by derived pullback. The right calculus of fractions and inversion of quasi-isomorphisms are the recorded homotopy localization instances.

For each resolution s:R→X, naturality and equality with the local component at R give β_X=L(s) inverse;r_R;L(s). All three factors are invertible, so β assembles to a natural automorphism. Substitution of its component equations at the telescope and its translate gives the required gauge identity.
